_meta.description: RING_OSC (ring_osc/RING_OSC.gds/.sch) <-> chip top-level pin connection plan, for integrating the two 97-stage (95x INV_X1/INV3D + AND2_X1 enable-gate + 1x INV_X1 output buffer) ring oscillators into src/tr_1um_i2c_slave_async.gds (v9 final chip, NOT the old v7-era _routed.gds -- confirmed with user). Status: PLACEMENT-ONLY staged, routing not yet done -- see status field below.

ring_osc_pins._comment: from ring_osc/RING_OSC.sch's top-level pins (ipin/opin/iopin), in schematic order

ENB.role: shared enable for BOTH rings (single pin, both AND2_X1 gates tied to the same ENB net -- see open_questions)

connections.VDD: chip VDD (not yet routed -- see open_questions)
connections.VSS: chip VSS (not yet routed -- see open_questions)

chip_top_pin_layout_coords_reference._comment: measured directly from src/tr_1um_i2c_slave_async.gds this session (TXM2(49,0) text layer), for later routing planning. Two coordinate pairs per pin: chip-side (near core/PTECT) and pad-side (near the physical bond pad, further out).

placement.orientation: r0 (no rotation, no mirror) -- assumed; not explicitly specified by user
placement.ptect_note: RING_OSC's absolute footprint at this origin is ENTIRELY inside the PTECT keepout area (layer 63/1) that all prior GIO<->core routing in this project has avoided (design_notes.md 78.x/79.x). Flagged to the user via AskUserQuestion 2026-08-31; user chose to proceed (originally at Y=-600, revised to Y=-650 in a later message -- 'Y=-650のことです。' -- both accept the same PTECT overlap). Also noted: the clear channel between PTECT's bottom edge (Y=-800) and the P9/P10 pad landing points (Y=-921.8) is only ~122um, less than RING_OSC's own height (244.8um), so shifting straight down to clear PTECT is not simply possible without a wider redesign.
placement.note_2026_08_31: origin_y revised from -600.0 to -650.0 (user: '1. Yを-50します' clarified as 'Y=-650のことです。' after AskUserQuestion flagged that -50 would overlap the core cell itself); re-run via script/place_ring_osc.py, no core overlap, PTECT overlap unchanged in kind (still fully inside).

power_routing._comment: step 2 of integration, this session, user: 'コアの両端のTAP2のM2をそのままRING_OSCまで延伸します。RING_OSCの上下にM1(10um)でVDD/VSSをつなぎます。配線まで進めてください。' -- implemented by script/route_ring_osc_power_v9.py, output ring_osc/tr_1um_i2c_slave_async_ringosc_routed.gds. REVISED after real KLayout DRC (ring_osc/DRC_error.lyrdb) found shorts in the M1 top/bottom bus feature; user instruction: '上下のM1の電源バーがショートしています。RING_OSCの上下にM1(10um)でVDD/VSSの接続はやめます。' -- the M1 bus feature has been removed entirely, see below.
power_routing.method: RING_OSC.gds already carries its own complete internal VDD/VSS mesh (2 dedicated 3.4um-wide M2 straps per end column, full RING_OSC height, tied into all 5 row power rails via pre-existing vias -- confirmed by direct via_1-cut (layer 19/0) inspection, not assumed). Its end-column strap X centerlines land EXACTLY on the core's own TAP0/TAP3 VDD/VSS strap centerlines once placed at the same X origin as the core (verified to the 0.1um: TAP0 VDD=-801.9/VSS=-807.3, TAP3 VDD=807.3/VSS=801.9). So the core's 2 end-column TAP2 M2 straps were extended with a straight M2 wire (no jog) from the core's own bbox bottom (Y=-140.0) down to Y=-545.0, landing solidly inside RING_OSC's own pre-existing top strap segment -- feeding RING_OSC's entire internal mesh, both rings, all rows, from this single connection at each end. This M2 strap extension is now the ONLY power routing this integration adds.
power_routing.m1_top_bottom_bus_REMOVED: A first version added 3 extra 10um-wide M1 buses (VSS+VDD at the top edge, VSS at the bottom edge) tied into the M2 straps via new vias, matching the core's own VDD_BUS_Y/VSS_BUS_Y convention. The user ran real DRC on this (ring_osc/DRC_error.lyrdb) and found 22 relevant violations (12x V1.S1 via-cut spacing <1.5, 4x V1.CO via-contact spacing <1.0, 6x M2.S1 M2 spacing <2.0), all at the 6 new bus-to-strap via junctions. Root cause: those junctions used multi_via()'s default HORIZONTAL 2-via offset on a narrow (3.4um) strap with only a 2.0um-spaced same-polarity neighbor -- exactly the situation route_gio_core_v9.py's own TAP_STUB_W/multi_via_v comments already documented and solved (with a VERTICAL via offset instead) for the core's own equivalent TAP-to-busbar junctions; this script's new bus vias didn't follow that precedent. User's decision, given directly: drop the M1 bus feature rather than fix it (`RING_OSCの上下にM1(10um)でVDD/VSSの接続はやめます`). script/route_ring_osc_power_v9.py has been rewritten to draw ONLY the M2 strap extension; the routed GDS was regenerated and a klayout.db self-check confirmed the M2-only version reproduces none of the 22 violations (VDD/VSS strap spacing is a clean 2.0um, matching the design's own existing minimum elsewhere, no vias added at all).
power_routing.verification_done: (1) Real KLayout DRC run by the user on the first (M1-bus) version -- found and diagnosed the 22 via/M1-bus-junction violations above, root-caused after the fact. (2) klayout.db self-check on the CURRENT (M2-only) routed GDS: VDD- and VSS-net M2 strap regions have zero overlap area, 2.0um minimum spacing maintained, and the new M2 strap extension geometrically continues into (not just touches) RING_OSC's own pre-existing native strap segment at both ends. (3) The routed GDS has not yet been re-run through the real DRC tool after this revision -- see open_questions.
power_routing.not_yet_done: Real DRC has not been re-run on the M2-only routed GDS (expected clean based on the self-check, but not yet confirmed by the actual tool). No LVS/connectivity extraction including RING_OSC's power nets. Signal routing (OUT->P9, OUTD->P10, ENB->P15) not started at all -- see open_questions. Two unrelated GC.ANT (gate antenna) violations from the DRC run, at abs X~710-713, appear pre-existing in RING_OSC's own native layout (unrelated to this power routing, all of which sits at abs X~800-810) -- not addressed here, left for the user's attention.

signal_routing._comment: step 3, this session, after user confirmed 'PTECTを修正してDRCクリーンを確認しました。配線を進めてください。' Implemented by script/route_ring_osc_signals_v9.py, output ring_osc/tr_1um_i2c_slave_async_ringosc_signals.gds. User confirmed via AskUserQuestion to extend route_gio_core_v9.py's own ring/corner-waypoint STYLE (M1 horizontal / M2 vertical, via_1 PCell at each layer transition) rather than a from-scratch scheme.
signal_routing.pin_locations_measured: Direct klayout.db text-layer scan of ring_osc/RING_OSC.gds, layer 48/0 (carries the schematic PORT name, distinct from layer 49/0's generic per-instance A/Y/vdd/gnd labels). Native-local: OUT M1 box (1608.2,28.0)-(1620.0,31.4); OUTD M1 box (1608.2,-26.6)-(1620.0,-23.2); ENB M1 riser (11.8,-116.3)-(14.4,-100.9) landing on an M2 bus (11.8,-118.9)-(1518.4,4.2) that distributes ENB to both AND2_X1 gates internally. At placement origin (-810,-650): OUT=(804.1,-620.3), OUTD=(804.1,-674.9), ENB=(-796.9,-750.9) (using the riser's less-congested upper end).
signal_routing.P15_is_rst_n: Important finding: P15 is not a spare pad -- schematic/v9_signal_routing_plan.json's own 'rst_n' entry has gio=(530,921.7,TOP,M2), matching P15 exactly, already routed from the core's own reset pin (305.1,794.6) via lane 10. Per the user's original wording ('ENBはP15(RSTN)につなぎます'), ENB is intentionally joining this SAME net -- so ENB's new wire is routed to physically merge with rst_n's own existing pad-side stub (abs (528.3,905.3)-(531.7,921.7) area) rather than needing an independent path to a truly empty pad.
signal_routing.routing_strategy: The existing 24-net shared lane system (route_gio_core_v9.py, LANE_R0=847 to 847+10*6=907, i.e. R=847..907, plus NEAR_R=913 for final per-pin spokes) was found by direct inspection to be essentially full -- e.g. a continuous M2 lane wire at abs X=851.3-854.7 spanning Y=-853..+330, and 9+ distinct M1 lane crossings spanning the whole top edge between Y=858 and Y=908. Rather than force 3 more nets into that band, each of OUT/OUTD/ENB was given its own individually-verified path in the SAME M1-horizontal/M2-vertical/via-at-turns style: an escape segment out through the ~22-24um-wide clear notch between RING_OSC/the core's own edge (abs X=+-816.3) and DIS_R=840's fixed ring (abs X=+-840) (X=824 for OUT, X=830 for OUTD, X=-822 for ENB), then a long run to a turn Y chosen OUTSIDE the lane band (Y=-913.0 for OUT, Y=-917.0 for OUTD -- both below the lane band's own Y range which mirrors to ~-908 -- and Y=852.0 for ENB, below the lane band's start at 858 on the top side), then a final horizontal run and a short vertical spoke landing exactly on each target pad's own X.
signal_routing.waypoints_SUPERSEDED_2026_08_31_round4: OUT->P9 and OUTD->P10 below were WRONG -- see revision_2026_08_31_round4 for the corrected OUT->OUT10 / OUTD->OUT9 routing. Kept here for history only.

waypoints.ENB->P15: (-796.5,-767.2)[M2 pin] -> (-796.5,-785.0)[M2, no via, clear of RING_OSC bbox] -> (-822.0,-785.0) -> (-822.0,852.0) -> (536.0,852.0) -> (536.0,907.0) -> (530.0,907.0)[merges into rst_n's own pre-existing M1 pad, exact Y-aligned; no separate via/M2 stub added -- see revision_2026_08_31_round3]

revision_2026_08_31_after_real_DRC._comment: user ran real DRC on the above version (ring_osc/DRC_error.lyrdb, 39 items) and asked: 'RING_OSCのLEFを作ってから再度挑戦ください。'
revision_2026_08_31_after_real_DRC.root_causes_found: Read DRC_error.lyrdb directly: 28x M2.W1 (M2 Wmin<3.0 -- M2_W had mistakenly been set to 1.8, copying M1's width), 5x M2.S1 + 2x M1.S1 + 2x M1.W1 (wire-meets-via T-junction notches, same class of bug route_gio_core_v9.py's own TAP_STUB_W comments already documented -- a wire narrower than the via_1 PCell's 3.4um pad creates a locally-narrow wing at the junction), 2x GC.ANT (unrelated, pre-existing in RING_OSC's own layout at abs X~710-713, not addressed).
revision_2026_08_31_after_real_DRC.lef_generated: script/gen_lef_ring_osc.py (new) generates ring_osc/RING_OSC.lef, following this project's own script/gen_lef.py convention (prBoundary->SIZE, M1PIN/M2PIN+TXM1/TXM2->PIN, remaining M1/M2 metal->OBS), adapted for RING_OSC being a hierarchical macro (pin/text scanning had to switch from recursive to DIRECT/non-recursive cell.each_shape(), since a recursive scan also picks up hundreds of internal per-instance A/Y pins from RING_OSC's ~400 std-cell sub-instances). Found RING_OSC.gds already has proper M1PIN/M2PIN markers for all 5 real ports -- no manual coordinate entry needed. Notable correction from the previous manual GDS-scanning approach: OUT/OUTD's real PIN rects are narrower than first assumed (1616.6-1620.0 local X, not 1608.2-1620.0), and ENB's real port is on M2 (not M1), at the very bottom edge (11.8,-118.9)-(15.2,-115.5) local -- the LEF is now the authoritative source for these, read via a small inline LEF-PIN parser in route_ring_osc_signals_v9.py.
revision_2026_08_31_after_real_DRC.routing_fixes: M1_W = M2_W = PAD = 3.4um uniformly (eliminates the T-junction notch class of violation and clears M2 Wmin=3.0). OUTD's top-side turn moved from Y=-917.0 to Y=-907.0 (the old value was only 1.3um from nearby unrelated pin stubs at Y=-920.0, under the 1.4 M1 minimum -- found by comparing width/space-check results before vs. after the width fix, since widening to 3.4 pushed the wire's edge closer to that obstacle). ENB's path gained 2 extra waypoints (a small X jog from 536->530 done specifically at Y=905.5, inside rst_n's own pad-stub band) after discovering ENB's final approach at X=530 ran parallel and too close (M2.S1) to an unrelated core signal's own C-spoke (abs X 524.8-528.2, Y 794.6-871) for the portion below Y=871 -- moving the merge-in point above that obstacle's own top edge (and inside the zone that's rst_n's own metal anyway, so it's an intentional same-net overlap there) resolved it.
revision_2026_08_31_after_real_DRC.verification_done: Same 3-way collision self-check as before (0 collisions), PLUS a new, more rigorous check this revision added: klayout.db's own width_check()/space_check() DRC primitives run on the merged M1/M2 regions, comparing the ROUTED-signals GDS against the pre-signal-routing base GDS to isolate ONLY violations introduced by this script. Result: 0 new M1 width, 0 new M2 width, 0 new M1 spacing, 0 new M2 spacing violations. (The base GDS itself has some pre-existing width/spacing flags under this same check, unrelated to this work -- not investigated further here.) SUPERSEDED by revision_2026_08_31_round2 below -- this check didn't cover via-cut (V1) spacing, which is exactly where the round-2 real DRC found a violation.

revision_2026_08_31_round2._comment: user ran real DRC again (ring_osc/DRC_error.lyrdb, now 2 items) and reported: '惜しい、P15の配線です。' -- i.e. close, but still a real issue specifically in the ENB->P15 wiring.
revision_2026_08_31_round2.root_cause_found: Read DRC_error.lyrdb directly: 1x V1.S1 (via-cut Smin<1.5), edge-pair (529.3,906.2)-(530.7,906.3) -- a 1.4um-wide sliver with only a 0.1um gap. Direct GDS query at that location (layer 19/0, the via-cut layer) confirmed TWO separate via cuts: the round-1 revision's own new via at (530,905.5), and an ALREADY-EXISTING via at ~(530,907.0) that is part of rst_n's own pre-existing M1-pad-stub -> via -> M2-riser -> P15 chain. Only 1.5um center-to-center (1.4um cut + 0.1um gap, vs. the 1.5um Smin the cut-to-cut gap itself needs). Root cause: (530,905.5) sits INSIDE rst_n's own pre-existing M1 pad-stub band (528.3,905.3)-(531.7,908.7), which already has its own via up to its own M2 riser continuing to P15 -- so ENB's M1 wire landing there already merges (M1-M1) onto that same net without needing a second, separate via right next to the existing one. The round-1 revision added a redundant via + M2 stub past this point anyway, which is what collided. The 2nd DRC item (V1.CO overlap at ENB's own pin, abs (-797,-767.9)-(-796,-767.1)) was already present/expected there (the via landing at the ENB M2 pin) and is not a real problem -- it's the via correctly overlapping the LEF-declared M2 pin box itself, consistent with every other pin-side via in this routing; not a new class of issue.
revision_2026_08_31_round2.routing_fix: script/route_ring_osc_signals_v9.py: ENB's route_path() waypoint list now ENDS at (530.0,905.5) -- the via and the final M2 segment up to P15 (530,921.8) have been removed entirely. The M1 wire from (536,905.5) to (530,905.5) already lands inside/merges with rst_n's own pre-existing M1 pad polygon (confirmed inside the P15 landing box (526,903,534,979)), and that pad's OWN pre-existing via + M2 riser already completes the electrical path up to P15 -- so no new via or M2 metal is needed at all at this final step.

revision_2026_08_31_round3._comment: user viewed the round-2 GDS directly in KLayout and reported 2 more real issues: 'RING_OSCのENBがVSSとショートしています。M1の引き出しがBBOXの内部にあるのが原因です。P15との接続もY軸が少し(1.5um)ズレています。'
revision_2026_08_31_round3.root_cause_1_ENB_VSS_short: route_path() used to drop a via right at the ENB pin itself ((-796.5,-767.2)) to transition from the pin's native M2 onto M1 for the leftward escape run. That via's M1 landing pad (PAD=3.4, centered exactly on the pin) lands squarely on a TAP cell's own M1 VSS metal there -- confirmed by direct GDS query on the pre-signal-routing base GDS: TAP2's own M1 at abs (-799.2,-768.9)-(-788.4,-750.9) fully contains the via's M1 pad footprint, an M1-M1 short to VSS. This was invisible to every self-check so far because ENB's own pin box is one of the LANDING_BOXES deliberately excluded from collision checking (on the assumption any overlap there is the intended pin merge -- true for the M2 side, false for the M1 side once a via is added). Further queries confirmed the entire X~-802..-790 column is densely packed with per-row TAP-cell M1 for the full row height, so no nearby in-bbox via location is safe either.
revision_2026_08_31_round3.fix_1: Generalized route_path(): it now only drops a via at the pin if the FIRST waypoint segment's own inferred layer actually differs from pin_layer (previously hardcoded to 'always via if pin_layer != M1', ENB-specific and wrong once ENB's first move stays on M2). ENB's waypoint list was rewritten to start with a plain M2 vertical drop from the pin (X=-796.5 fixed, matching the pin's own layer, so NO via at all) down to Y=-785.0 -- clear of RING_OSC's own bbox (bottom edge Y=-770.0) and clear of the two vertical VDD/VSS M2 straps (X=-801.9/-807.3, well away from X=-796.5, so a purely vertical move there never touches them). The via + M1 escape run to X=-822.0 now happen at Y=-785.0, fully outside RING_OSC's footprint -- confirmed by direct GDS query: 0.0 um^2 overlap on BOTH M1 and M2 at both new via locations ((-796.5,-785.0) and (-822.0,-785.0)) against the pre-signal-routing base GDS. The M1 run crossing the VDD/VSS strap X positions at this Y is a harmless M1-over-M2 crossover (no via placed there), not a merge.
revision_2026_08_31_round3.root_cause_2_P15_Y_offset: Round 2's landing Y (905.5) undershot rst_n's own real pre-existing M1 pad-stub. Direct query on the pre-signal-routing base GDS shows the pad's true M1 footprint is abs (305.1,905.3)-(531.7,908.7) -- NOT (305.1,903.8)-(537.7,908.7) as it appeared when queried on the POST-routing GDS (that wider footprint was an artifact of ENB's own M1_W=3.4 wire at Y=905.5 protruding 1.5um below the pad's real bottom edge, 905.3-903.8=1.5, and merging with/widening the query result). The pad's own pre-existing via (found in round 2) sits at Y=907.0, i.e. the pad is exactly centered there (905.3 to 908.7, height 3.4).
revision_2026_08_31_round3.fix_2: Moved ENB's final landing Y from 905.5 to 907.0 (and the preceding turn at X=536 to the same Y). The M1 wire (width 3.4) now spans Y 905.3-908.7, an exact match to the pre-existing pad's own footprint with zero protrusion in either direction -- confirmed by direct query: the overlap region between the new landing wire and the pre-existing base M1 is exactly (530.0,905.3)-(531.7,908.7), i.e. the pad's own bounds, nothing more.

revision_2026_08_31_round4._comment: user reviewed the real LVS result and reported: '配線ミスです。RINGOSC(OUT)＞P10、RINGOSC(OUTD)＞VSS になっていますが、正しくは RINGOSC(OUT)＞OUT10、RINGOSC(OUTD)＞OUT9です。念のためLVS_error.lvsdbを確認ください。' Then, separately: 'spice も間違っています。JSONを修正ください。'
revision_2026_08_31_round4.root_cause_found: OUT and OUTD were routed directly onto the RAW P9/P10 bond-pad nets, bypassing OSS_FRAME_GIO's own dedicated driver-INPUT pins (OUT9/OUT10) that feed each pad's internal tri-state output buffer -- the same pattern every other real output signal in this chip uses (e.g. sda's own 'SDA_O' net feeds into GIO, it doesn't tie straight to a P-numbered pad). Worse, the OLD OUT target (200.0,-921.8) turns out to not even be P9's own location: direct GDS text-label queries (layer 49/0, TXM2) show P9's real signal-level pin is at abs (270,-921.8), while (200,-921.8) sits right on top of that pad group's own GND/VSS pin label ('GND'/'gnd' text confirmed at (200,-921.7) and (200,-932.2)) -- so OUT's old routing was actually landing on GND, a real short, matching the 'OUTD>VSS'-type symptom the user reported (exact OUT/OUTD labeling in the user's own LVS browser view may differ from this script's internal naming, but the underlying physical short is the same one independently confirmed here). LEF/OSS_FRAME_GIO.lef gives the correct locations once its own ORIGIN(1250,1250) offset is applied: OUT9 PIN native (1428.3,326.6)-(1431.7,330.0) -> abs (178.3,-923.4)-(181.7,-920.0); OUT10 PIN native (1868.3,326.6)-(1871.7,330.0) -> abs (618.3,-923.4)-(621.7,-920.0) -- both M2, confirmed by direct GDS text-label cross-check (OUT9 label at (180,-922.6), OUT10 at (620,-922.6)).
revision_2026_08_31_round4.pad_assignment_swap: Per the user's explicit correction, the pairing also SWAPS relative to the old (wrong) scheme: RING_OSC's OUT (first ring) now targets OUT10 (abs X=620) -- eventually driving pad P10 through GIO's own buffer -- and OUTD (second ring) now targets OUT9 (abs X=180) -- eventually driving pad P9. This is the opposite of the old OUT->(near P9 by intent)/OUTD->P10 pairing.
revision_2026_08_31_round4.routing_fix: script/route_ring_osc_signals_v9.py: OUT now escapes via X=830 (the old OUTD-style corridor) to turn Y=-907.0 then lands at (620.0,-921.7) on OUT10; OUTD now escapes via X=824 (the old OUT-style corridor) to turn Y=-913.0 then lands at (180.0,-921.7) on OUT9 -- i.e. the two paths' escape corridors were swapped to match each signal's new (and roughly mirrored) destination, verified individually clear via direct GDS overlap queries at every via/segment (0.0 um^2 unintended overlap on both M1 and M2 at all 4 new via locations). ENB->P15 routing is unchanged.
